chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the meal is presented, and a man from them has named (Bismillah), it suffices for them altogether.'
ai.seo_question: Does one person's Bismillah suffice for everyone eating together?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishing the principle of 'ta'abbud' (divine acceptance) for communal meals, where a single Bismillah suffices for the group. This reflects the Shia juristic view that the primary obligation lies in the initial invocation, fostering unity and simplicity in shared dining etiquette. The hadith underscores the spiritual significance of acknowledging God’s name as the gateway to the blessing of food for all present.
